title: A first collaboration conversation: Snap25 Foundation and STXBP1 Foundation

sentences.text: We would welcome a careful collaboration that keeps families’ needs at its heart.
SNAP25 and STXBP1 help nerve cells release chemical messages, and reviews group their disorders in the same disease family.
An altered protein blocking the working protein is a possible shared mechanism, but the STXBP1 evidence is contested.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: CMDIR, Simons Searchlight and RARE-X already include people with SNAP25-related disorders.
Citizen Health and the ENDD Center offer STXBP1-related resources worth exploring together.
Could we compare experiences with these resources before creating anything new?

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please confirm whether Citizen Health, ENDD and ESCO accept related conditions rather than assuming their resources transfer directly.

Check whether repeated speech (echolalia), weakness that worsens with use, and knees fixed in a bent position occur in STXBP1-related disorders, and clarify the nine additional symptom gaps flagged for resource comparisons.
Please review differences involving unstable or misfolded proteins and assembly of the message-release machinery called the SNARE complex.
Read both sides of the contested STXBP1 mechanism evidence before relying on it.
Could Ege Kavalali review the plan, including model access and the effects of individual variants?
Send STXBP1 Foundation one focused inquiry asking whether STARR (STXBP1 Clinical Trial Ready), the natural history study, could include SNAP25-related disorders.
Is there a documented, accessible animal or cell model for SNAP25-related disorders in the atlas?
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired—less able to carry out their chemical task—or loss of function?
Please check model access through MGI, JAX, hPSCreg, EBiSC and linked researchers, and seek SNAP25-specific functional evidence for variants.
Dear STXBP1 Foundation team,
Could we explore whether STARR could include SNAP25-related disorders?
Our disorders share nerve-cell message-release biology, although the proposed shared protein-blocking mechanism remains contested for STXBP1.
We would welcome an initial eligibility check, without assuming that inclusion is possible.
Thank you for considering this small first step together.
[Your name], on behalf of Snap25 Foundation
